KVKs in Karnataka 
* 383. SHRI H.K. JAVARE GOWDA: Will the Minister of 
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Karnataka Government has requested the Central 
Government to sanction new Krishi Vigyan Kendras in eleven districts; and 
(b) if so, what steps are proposed to be taken by Government to establish 
Krishi Vigyan Kendras in the newly formed districts of that State? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI AJIT SINGH): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) There are seven newly formed dist ricts in Karnataka.  Out of which, 
Gadag and Haveri districts have Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVK). The Zonal 
Agricultural Research Station (ZARS) in Udupi district has been stregthened 
to take up the additional functions of KVK under National Agricultural 
Technology Project (NATP). Other four new districts, viz., Chamarajanagara, 
Koppal, Bagalkote and Devanagre are covered with the existing KVK^ZARSs 
in the original districts from which these have been newly created.

RAJYA SABHA [19 April, 2002] 
Standard of school education 
† * 384. SHRIMATI SAVITA SHARDA : Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that standard of school education in various parts of 
the country is deteriorating day by day; 
(b) if so, whether Government are considering to take any steps for 
improving the same; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) it not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. 
MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) to (d) "E ducation" is in the Concurrent 
List of the Constitution, and manage ment and academic arrangements in 
schools are primarily the concern of St ate/UT Governments. Information is 
received from time-to-time that quality of  education is deteriorating at some 
places. National Policy of Education, 1986 (as modified in 1992) has laid 
special emphasis on quality of education. In pursuance of the policy, the 
Central Government has been emphasizing the need to constantly improve 
the quality of education. 
A number of schemes are being implemented for improving quality of 
primary/elementary education in cooperation with the State/UT Governments. 
District Primary Education Programme (DPEP) is a holistic programme for 
development of primary education. The programme at present covers 273 
districts in 18 States. The project provides several interventions for quality 
improvement. These inter- 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
4 

[19 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
ventions include textbooks development, teacher training, capacity building, 
supply of teaching learning materials, appointment of additional teachers, 
improvement in the school environment etc. In all the DPEP States, new 
textbooks have been developed and several rounds of improved teacher training 
have been conducted. New ins titutions of Block Resource Centres and Cluster 
Resource Centres have been established to provide academic resource support at 
sub-district levels. A joint Government of India — United Nations programme 
namely, Jan Shala is being implemented in 105 blocks in 9 States. It is a 
community-based programme, which aims at improving the quality of 
primary education. 
A new scheme of Sarva Shikha Abhiyan has been launched with the 
objective of providing quality elementary education to all the children in 6—14 
age group by 2010. District Elementary Education Plans have been sanctioned 
under the scheme for 512 districts for the year 2001-2002. The scheme of 
Restructuring and Reorganisation of  Teacher Education is being implemented 
to create a viable institutional infrastructure, academic and technical resource bas 
orientation, training and continuous up gradation of know] competence and 
pedagogical skills of school teachers in the country. So far, 470 District Institutes 
of Educational Training have been sanctioned and more than 16 lakhs teachers 
trained under this scheme. 
In the field of Secondary Education, a number of Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes like Computer Literacy and Studies in Schools (CLASS), 
Improvement of Science Education in Schools, Environmental Orientation to 
School Education etc. are being implemented for improving the quality of 
education.

Nutritious Noon Meal Scheme in States 
† * 386. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the Nutritious Noon Meal Scheme 
of the, Tamil Nadu Government; 
(b) if so, whether Government propose to introduce such schemes all over 
the country, through their financial assistance; 
(c) if not, whether Government would also assist financially such schemes 
in States where it is already existing; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. 
MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) to (d) The Central Government has already launched the National 
Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (popularly called the 
Mid-Day Meal Scheme) in August 1995, under which foodgrains are made 
available free of cost to States/UTs for children of primary classes (I-V) in 
Government, local bodies and Government aided schools. Transportation 
charges also being reimbursed to State agencies. The cost of conversion of 
foodgrains into cooked meals is to be met by the States/Implementing 
Agencies.

Parent-Teacher Associations in KVS 
* 387.    SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN: 
     SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:  
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Academic Advisory Committee, at its 19th 
meeting held on 22nd November, 2001, took a decision to modify the process of 
election of members of the Parent-Teacher Associations in Kendriya Vidyalayas, 
substituting the democratic right of election by nomination by the Vidyalaya 
Management Committee; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether the Federation of Kendriya Vidyalaya P.T.As, Kerala, has passed a 
resolution requesting the Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan to withdraw such 
amendment/modification; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. 
MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) and (b) The guidelines for Parents Teachers 
Association in Kendriya Vidyalayas had a contradiction as clause 8 provided that 
all members of the Executive Committee will be nomin ated by the Chairman, 
VMC, whereas Clause 16 while giving details of the business to be transacted in 
the Annual Meeting of the General Body, provided for election of the office 
bearers and Committee members of the A ssociation. The Academic Advisory 
Committee has removed this contradiction by deleting Clause 16 (iv) of the said 
guidelines. 
(c) and (d) A resolution to this effect  had been received from federation of 
Kendriya Vidyalaya PTAs, Kerala State. The federation has thereafter filed a 
petition in High Court of Kerala and the matter is subjudice.

Mobile Police Posts in trains 
* 388.    SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: 
SHRI RUMANDLA RAMACHANDRAIAH: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Railways are considering to provide mobile police posts on 
24 express trains/passenger trains to check the activities of inter-State dacoit 
gangs, committing various offences and terrorising passengers, by resorting to 
looting; 
(b) if so, in which trains; 
(c) by when this proposal is likely to be implemented; 
(d) whether this would give greater confidence to the passengers; 
(e) whether new personnel would be recruited for this purpose; 
(f) whether further protection is being considered for rail passengers; and 
(g) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI NITISH KUMAR): (a) No, Sir. 
Maintenance of law and order on Railways is the responsibility of the State; 
mobile police posts have already been provided by Government Railway 
Police on some of the trains in certain States. 
(b) to (e) Do not arise. 
(f) and (g) As per the recommendation of High Level Committee on 
security of Railways, the proposal to  empower the Railway Protection Force 
for providing better security to passe ngers is under examination. For this 
purpose amendments to RPF Act 1957 and Railways Act 1989 are under 
consideration.

RAJYA SABHA [19 April, 2002] 
Navodaya Colleges 
* 389. SHRI BACHANI LEKHRAJ: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to set up Navodaya Colleges in the 
country, on the lines of Navodaya Vidyalayas; 
(b) if so the details thereof; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. 
MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) to (c) Cl ause 5.26 of the National Policy 
on Education lays down that in view of the need to effect an all round 
improvement in the institutions, in the near future, the main emphasis will be 
on the consolidation of, and expansion of facilities in, the existing 
institutions. Therefore, there is no proposal on the part of the Government to 
set up Navodaya Colleges in the Country. 
Conservation of coastal and marine environment 
* 390. PROF. M. SANKARALINGAM: Will the Minister of 
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to prepare an action plan for 
conservation of coastal and marine environment; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the details of achievements made by Government in this field during 
the last five years? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. 
BAALU): (a) to (d) Ministry of Environment and Forests launched a Scheme 
on Conservation and Management of Mangroves and Coral Reefs in 1986. 
On the recommendations of the National 
12 

[19 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
Committee on Mangroves and Coral Reefs, 30 Mangrove and 4 Coral Reef 
areas in the country have  been identified for intensive conservation and 
management. Management Action Plans for all the identified Mangrove and 
Coral Reef areas were prepared and an amount of Rs. 1317.28 lakhs was 
released to the concerned State Governments/Union Territories for 
implementation of these Management Action Plans during the Ninth Five 
Year Plan. As per the State of Forest s Report (1999) an overall increase of 
338 sq. km. of mangrove area in the country has been reported during the 
period 1995—1999.  
This Ministry has also launched an All India Co-ordinated Project on 
Coastal and Marine Bio-diversity during the year 1999-2000. Main activities 
under this project include Survey and inventorisation. Training and Capacity 
Building in Taxonomy and Establishment of Database Network on the subject. 
The Coastal Shelterbclt Plantation Projects under integrated Afforestation and 
Eco-Development Project Scheme (IAEPS) envisage plantation in rows 
along the coastline to create a shelterbelt for checking soil erosion and sand 
ingress for protection of agricultural fields, homesteads, roads etc. To 
conserve and protect fragile coastal ecosystems. Ministry of Environment and 
Forests issued Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification, 1991 under the 
Environmental Protection Act (1986). Coastal Zone Management Authorities 
(CZMAs) have been constituted in all the coastal States/Union territories to 
ensure implementation of the provisions of the CRZ Notification, 1991. 
Coral Reefs have been included in Schedule 1 of the Wildlife Protection Act 
1972. Sunderbans in West Bengal, Gulf of Mannar in Tamil Nadu and 
Nicobar Islands have been designated as Bio-sphcre Reserves. Department 
of Ocean Development (DOD) has also launched a programme on Integrated 
Coastal and Marine Area Management (ICMAM) during the Ninth Plan 
period.

Railway corporation for Chennai MRTS 
* 391. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: W ill the Minister of RAILWAYS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether any proposal for setting up of a separate railway corporation 
for Chennai Mass Rapid Transport System is under consideration; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI NITISH KUMAR): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) Does not arise.  
(c) Setting up of a separate corporation has not been felt necessary 
so far due to following reasons:—  
(i) Phase I from Chennai Beach to Tiru mailai is under operation with the 
train services integrated with the suburban services of the Southern 
Railway. 
(ii) Construction of Phase II of the Chennai Mass Rapid Transit System 
from Tirumailai to Vclachari is under execution on cost sharing basis 
between the Railways and State Government of Tamil Nadu. Both 
the Governments have been providing requisite funds for construction 
of the system. The project has been making satisfactory progress with 
the existing arrangement. 
(hi) State Government has not come forward with any proposal in this 
regard.

(a) whether it is a fact that the beauty of lakes in the country is vanishing 
due to non-cleaning of lakes particul arly those close to tourist places, and 
rapidly increasing tendency of poaching the birds; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether   it    is    a    fact    that    the    amount    allocated    by

THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. 
BAALU): (a) to (c) The lakes, specially those near the tourist places, have 
become polluted to varying degrees due to siltation, encroachments and 
discharge of domestic and industrial effluents. This has resulted in 
eutrophication, weed infestation, decrease in biological diversity particularly 
endemic and endangered species, decrease in migratory bird population and 
fish productivity. 
The Government in 1994 had formulated National Lake Conservation 
Plan (NLCP) under which 10 urban polluted lakes were identified for 
conservation. The lakes identified under NLCP arc as follows:—

from cultivating foodgrains to oilseeds, as about 40 per cent of c ountry's

Direct purchase of cotton from growers 
2776. SHRIMATI VANG A GEETHA: Will the Minister of 
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to purchase cotton directly from the 
cotton growers, and eliminate middlemen between the farmers and CCI; and 
(b) the action taken to assist the cotton farmers in ensuring reasonable 
prices of cotton produced? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) The Cotton Corporation of 
India (CCI), a Central nodal agency, makes purchases directly from Cotton 
growers in the regulated market. CCI extends its infrastructure by utilizing 
the Co-operative set up in each State.

Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for different varieties of cotton during each 
season and authorizes the CCI to undertake price support operation if market 
prices touch MSP level, (ii) hiked the import duty on cotton from 5 per cent 
to 10 per cent to restrain import, (iii) made cotton export free with effect 
from July, 2001 dispensing with the earlier export quota of different agencies 
and the

Commissioner, Mumbai, and (iv) launched the Technology Mission on

SFAC Scheme 
2778. DR. DASARI NARAYANA RAO: Will the Minister of 
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are implementing the Central Sector Scheme, 
namely setting up of Small Farmers Agri-Busincss Consortium (SFAC); 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Andhra Pradesh has formed the State level SFAC; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof?  
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The Central Sector Scheme provides Grants-in-Aid to the Small 
Farmers Agri-Business Consortium (SFAC), which is a Public—Private 
Joint Venture Society , declared as a financial Institution under section 
17(8A) of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934 and under Section 
9(l)(c) of the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) Act, 1964. It was 
registered on the 18th January, 1994, under the Societies Registration Act, 
1860, as a Society by the Ministry of Agriculture, Department of Agriculture 
and Co-operation. It has a diverse membership, with the Department of 
Agriculture and Co-operation, Reserve Bank of India (RBI), IDBI, National 
Bank for Agriculture & Rural Development (NABARD), State Bank of India 
(SBI) and Oriental Bank of Commerce (OBC) being the Promoter Members, 
and Canara Bank, 
45 
 

RAJYA SABHA [19 April, 2002] 
National Agricultural Co-operative Marketing Federation of India Limited 
(NAFED) and M/s United Phosphorous Ltd. (a private company) as its 
primary members. Other banks, Financial institutions, Statutory and 
Autonomous Organizations, dealing in agriculture and agro industries, private 
companies and co-operatives, exporters, NGO/farmcrs organizations working 
in rural areas, and beneficiaries, including individual farmers can also 
become members of this society at the national level. State level counterpart 
Societies have been registered by 13 States so far to take advantage of the 
Schemetic Pattern of Assistance of the (Central) SFAC in its functions. 
(c) No, Sir. 
(d) Does not arise. 
Incentives for cashew growers 
2779. SHRI H.K. JAVARE GO WDA: Will the Minister of 
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that cashew farmers are facing falling prices 
of their produce and extreme-compe titive atmosphere caused by the 
WTO regime; 
(b) if so, what step Government propose to take to save the cashew 
farmers; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that ther e is a great demand for originally 
produced cashew from western countries; and 
(d) if so, whether Government propose to give special packages for 
Karnataka cashew growers; if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) The price of raw 
cashew-nut is influenced by the international price of cashew kernel. Though 
there has been some decrease in the 
 
46 

[19 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
international price of cashew kernel during 2001-02, the Indian price 
of raw cashew-nut during the period has been higher than the 
prevailing rates during 1997-98 and 1998-99. Under the Centrally 
sponsored Scheme on Macro Management in

work plans assistance is being provided to the farmers for various activities

Construction and commercial production of fertilizer units 
2806. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS 
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) the reasons for which fertilizer plants in the cooperative sector are in 
profit, whereas the PSU fertilizer units arc in losses; 
(b) whether Government have invested money in any fertilizer units on 
their erection and are paying salaries to employees but they have not started 
commercial production of fertilizer for the last several years; 
(c) if so, the names of the units, when they were constructed and how 
much money has been spent; and 
(d) the reasons for not starting commercial production by them? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS 
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI SATYA BRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) The 
profitability of fertilizer plants depe nds upon the various factors such as 
vintage of plant, technology, feedstock, product profile, human resources, 
managerial expertise, sources of finance and many other factors within the 
control of management. The cooperative sector plants have an advantage in 
some of these areas vis-a-vis some PSUs, making them profitable. However, 
some of the fertilizer PSUs such as Ra shtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers Ltd. 
(RCF) and National Fertilizers Ltd. (NFL) too are making profits. 
(b) to (d) The Haldia Fertilizer Project of Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation 
Ltd. (HFC), which was mechanically completed in the end of 1979 could 
never be commissioned due to insufficient quantum of power sanctioned by 
West Bengal State Electricity Bo ard and breakdown of number of 
equipments. Thereafter, various alternatives were explored to revive the 
project, but its revamp was not found to be techno-economically viable. The 
cost of Haldia Project was Rs. 520.90 crore as in April, 1986.

preventing human killings by leopards are—

the top priority area of concern in a National State of Environment Report, 
prepared for the United Nations Environment Programme, to be considered

108

identified, priorities allocated and practical steps outlines, to correct the 
growing environmental imbalances? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. 
BAALU): (a) to (c) The State of the Environment Report prepared for India 
for the forthcoming Earth Summit 2002 broadly covers five priority issues 
pertaining to the environment. These issues include land degradation, bio-
diversity, air pollution with special reference to vehicular pollution in cities, 
management of fresh water resources and hazardous waste management with 
special reference to municipal solid waste management. However, in the  
priority area of air pollution, top priority is given to vehicular pollution as 
70% of air pollution is from vehicular emissions in the metropolitan cities of 
the country. The details of the practical strategies as outlines in the report to 
check the rising air pollution level, especially in the metropolitan cities, 
include the following: 
• The measure to control vehicular pollution include promotion of public 
transport and mass rapid transport systems together with traffic 
planning and management, taxes on fuels and vehicles, stringent 
emission norms and fuel quality specifications, promotion of cleaner 
fuels such as CNG, replacement of two-stroke engines, and a 
strengthening of the inspection and maintenance (I&M) system. 
• Measures to control industrial air pollution include promotion of 
cleaner technologies, st rengthening of emission standards. introducing 
economic incentives, strengthening of the monitoring and reporting 
system, waste minimisation and utilisation and appropriate sitting of 
industries so as to minimise the impacts of activities on ecosystems and 
human health. 
• Formulation of a comprehensive urban air quality management strategy 
using information related to urban planning, ambient air quality, an 
emission inventory, and air quality dispersion models Strengthening 
the monitoring network and institutional capabilities to facilitate an 
improvement in the enforcement mechanism.

• Launching of the epidemiological studies to develop dose-response

RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:

250 colleges, of Assam;

(c) the procedure adopted by National Assessment and Accreditation 
Council (NAAC), to accrcditatc a college and select for UGC grants?

RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT [DR. (S HRIMATI) RITA VERMA]: (a) 
Yes, Sir.

voluntary till, 2000. There were also apprehensions regarding the 
assessment/accreditation process as the colleges were not aware of 
implications of the accreditation and its benefits. The National Assessment 
and Accreditation Council (NAAC) has already undertaken a number of 
awareness programme in collaboratio n with the State Government to

preparation of self study report by institutions/departments using defined

research, consultancy and extension, infrastructure, student support etc. The

Committee of NAAC.

Removal of KV Teachers Under Education Code CODE 
Article 81  (D).   Voluntary Abandonment of Service 
(1) If an employee has been ab sent/remains absent without 
sanctioned leave or beyond the period of leave originally 
granted or subsequently extended, he shall provisionally lose 
his lien on his post unless:—  
(a) he returns within fifteen calendar days of the commencement 
of the absence or the expiry of leave originally granted or 
subsequently extended, as the case may be; and 
(b) satisfies the appointing authority that his absence or his inability 
to return on the expiry of the leave as the case may be was for 
reasons beyond his control. The employee not reporting for duty 
within fifteen calendar days and satisfactorily explaining the 
reasons for such absence as afor esaid shall be deemed to have 
voluntarily abandoned his service and would thereby 
provisionally lose lien on his post. 
(2) An employee who has provisionally lost lien on his post in 
terms of the aforesaid provisions, shall not be entitled to the 
pay and allowances or any other benefit after he has 
provisionally lost lien on his post provided that payment of 
such pay and allowances will be regulated by such directions as 
150 

[19 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
the appointing authority may issue while ordering reinstatement of 
the employee in terms of Sub-clause (6) of this Article. 
(3) In cases falling under Sub-clause (1) of this Article, an order 
recording the factum of voluntary abandonment of service by the 
employee and provisional loss of his lien on the post, shall be made 
and communicated to the employee concerned at the address recorded 
in his service book and/or his last known address, to show cause why 
the provisional order above mentioned may not be confirmed. 
(4) The employee may make a written representation to the appointing 
authority, within ten days of r eceipt of the order made under Sub-
clause (3). 
(5) The appointing authority may on receipt of the representation, if any, 
and perusal of materials, available on record as also those submitted 
by the employee, grant, at his discretion, an oral hearing to the 
employee concerned to represent his case. 
(6) If the appointing authority is satisfied after such hearing that the 
employee concerned has voluntarily abandoned his service in terms of 
the provisions of Sub-clause (1) of th is Article, he shall pass an order 
confirming the loss of employee's lien on his post and in that event, 
the employee concerned shall be deemed to have been removed from 
the service of the Kendriya Vidyal aya Sangathan with effect from the 
date of his remaining absent. In case the appointing authority is 
satisfied that the provision of Sub-clause (1) of Clause (d) of this 
Article arc not attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case, he 
may order rc-instatcment of employee to the post last held by him, 
subject to such directions as he may give regarding the pay and 
allowances for the period of absence. 
(7) APPELLATE AUTHORITY: An employee aggrieved by an order 
passed under Sub-clause (6) of this Article may prefer an appeal to the 
Appellate Authority as notified by the Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan 
from time to time. 
151 

RAJYA SABHA [19 April, 2002] 
(8) PERIOD OF LIMITATION FOR APPEALS : No appeal preferred 
under this Article shall be entertained unless it is preferred within a period 
of 45 days from the date on which a copy of the order appealed against is 
served on the appellant provided that the Appellate Authority may entertain 
the appeal after the expiry of the said period, if it is satisfied that the 
appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from not preferring the appeal 
in time. 
(9) FORM AND CONTENTS OF APPEAL: Form and contents of appeal 
shall mutatis mutandis be the same as prescribed under the CCS (CCA) 
Rules 1965. 
(10) CONSIDERATION OF APPEAL:  The appellate authority 
shall consider: 
whether the requirements laid down under Sub-clause (1), (3), (5) and (6) 
of this Article have been complied with and, if not, whether such non-
compliance has resulted in failure of justice; 
whether the order confirming loss of employee's lien on his post and his 
consequent removal from service is warranted on record; and 
pass order confirming modifying or setting aside the order passed under 
Sub-clause (6) of this Article. 
(11) IMPLEMENTATION    OF    ORDER    OF    APPEAL:    The 
appointing authority shall give effect to the order passed by the 
Appellate Authority. 
(12) FINALITY OF ORDER PASSED IN APPEAL:  The order of the 
Appellate Authority made under this Article shall be final and shall not be 
called in question by way of any further application/petition for revision, 
review etc. 
(13) APPLICABILITY OF THE CCS (CCA) RULES: In matters falling 
under this Article and in those matters alone the procedure prescribed 
for holding inquiry in accordance with the CCS (Classification, Control & 
Appeal) Rules 1965 as applicable to the employees of the Kendriya 
Vidyalaya Sangathan as also other provisions of the said rules which arc 
not consistent with the provisions of this Article shall stand dispensed 
with.

(14) REMOVAL OF DIFFICULTIES: Notwithstanding anything contained 
in any rule or order for the time being in force in KVS, the 
Commissioner KVS may, with the approval of the Vice-Chairman, 
KVS issue such instructions as  he may deem fit to remove 
difficulties in the implementation of these provisions. 
(15) POWER TO ISSUE INSTRUCTIONS : Without prejudice to the 
generality of the foregoing provisions, the Commissioner, Kendriya 
Vidyalaya Sangathan may, with the approval of the Vice-Chairman, 
Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan, issue, from time to time (whether by 
way of relaxation of the aforesaid provisions or otherwise) general or 
special orders as to the guidelines, principles or procedures to be 
followed in giving effect to the provisions of this Article.

Health facilities to physically handicapped 
2876. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether health facilities are available for the physically 
handicapped, aged and children at main railway stations in the 
country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; station-wise; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the effective measures being taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL): (a) to (b) Health of the general public is not within 
the purview of Railways and is a subject dealt with by the State Governments. At 
railway stations, health services are not maintained for passengers. However, 
first aid facilities are available for emergencies for which a First Aid Box is 
available with the Assistant Station Master/Deputy Station Superintendent. 
Frontline railway staff are trained in providing first aid. Besides, Assistant Station 
Master/Deputy Station Superintendent maintains a list of medical practitioners and a 
list of nearby hospitals with particulars such as telephone numbers, distance from 
station etc. for availing treatment in emergency. No exclusive health care services 
are provided to the physically handicapped, aged and children at railway 
stations. Wheel chairs and stretchers are, however, provided at important stations 
for the convenience of physically handicapped and aged persons. Further, 
amenities for physically handicapped passengers like signages, ramps with railing for 
barrier free entry, low level water taps, user friendly toilets, non-slippery walkways, 
parking spaces have been/are being progressively provided at important stations 
subject to the availability of funds. The details of the same are given in the 
Statement.

Decongestion of saturated rail routes 
2892. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY: 
SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the news report, 
"Railway Panel wants saturated routes decongested", published in the Hindu 
dated the 13th March, 2002; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and Government's reaction thereto; 
(c) steps proposed to be taken in this regard; and 
(d) the amount of investment required to revamp the basic 
infrastructure, like routes? 
 186 

[19 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL): (a) to (d) Yes, Sir. The news report is regarding 
the recommendations contained in the Fourth Report of the Railway Convention 
Committee (1999) on Development of Alternative Routes for Decongesting 
Existing Routes. Highlighting the need to strengthen the Rail network on the 
Golden Quardrilateral and the two diagonals, the article has also brought out the 
precarious financial position of the Railways and the extremely thin spread of the 
available resources. The article has also talked about the need for a more 
rational use of the available resources and a concerted effort to explore all 
possible avenues for additional resources. 
The need to enhance line capacity on saturated routes in general, and on the 
Golden Quadrilateral in particular, is one of the priority areas for Indian Railways. 
In this regard, for following specific areas of investment have been identified: 
■ Doubling of remaining single line sections 
■ Additional lines on selected routes. 
■ Electrification of the unelectrified sections 
■ Grade separation at important road-rail crossings 
■ Signalling Improvements & Manning of Level Crossings. 
■ Increasing speed of freight trains to reduce speed differential between 
freight trains and Mail/Express trains. 
■ Introduction of High Horse Power Locomotives 
■ Track upgradation. 
The total requirement of funds for strengthening the Golden Quadrilateral on 
the above lines is approximately Rs. 16,000 Crores. 
A number of steps have also been taken to improve the resource availability and 
utilisation position. 
187 

RAJYA SABHA [19 April, 2002] 
• The probclm of large shelf of on going projects leading to thin spread of 
resources is more acute in respect of New Lines and Gauge Conversion 
projects. In order to enable judicious allocation of resources these 
projects have been prioritised on the basis of their operational requirements, 
physical progress, national and strategic importance and social desirability. 
• Special Railway Safety Fund of Rs. 17,000 Crores has been created to 
undertake renewal of overaged assets, which the Railways were unable to 
undertake in the normal course due to shortfall in internal generation. 
• By rationalizing the passenger fare in the current year's budget the resource 
base of the Railways is expected to be augmented by Rs. 910 crores. 
• In order to contain the staff costs, railways have been progressively 
reducing their staff strength. During the tenth Plan it is proposed to achieve 
2% reduction in staff strength every year. 
• Railways have already started drawing power directly from NTPC at a 
few locations. Railways arc also exploring the possibility of setting up 
captive power houses for generating electricity for traction purposes. These 
steps are likely to bring down high cost of electric traction. 
• Steps are being taken to involve the private sector and the State Governments in 
execution of Railway projects through financial participation by means of 
SPVs or through cost sharing. In addition projects are also sought to be 
executed through the BOT scheme.

2912. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Will the Minister of 
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:

country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any centre would be located in Rajasthan; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY IN THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND

Earthquake prone site of dam in Koyna 
2913. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAI AH: Will the Minister of 
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Koyna in Maharashtra where there is a large dam 
would be an earthquake prone site for the next 30 to 40 years; 
(b) if so, whether the dam is likely to withstand the earthquakes; and 
(c) if not, what steps are proposed to be taken in this regard? 
217 

RAJYA SABHA [19 April, 2002] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY IN THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI BACHI SINGH RAWAT): (a) As per seismic 
zoning map of India published by Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the Koyna 
Dam falls under zone IV. This zone is broadly associated with earthquakes of 
intensity up to VIII on the Modified Mercalli Scale. At present, there is no 
scientific technique available anywhere in the world which can prediet the 
earthquake with reasonable degree of accuracy in terms of time, sp ace and 
magnitude. It is therefore not possible to forecast earthquake activity in Koyna-
Warna region for the next 30—40 years. 
(b) The Koyna Dam has been suitably strengthened after the occurrence of 
1967 Koyna earthquake of Magnitude 6.3 on Ritcher scale to withstand future 
earthquakes. 
(c) The area is continuously monitored and various scientific 
studies/investigations have been taken up to understand the earthquake 
mechanism in the region.
